steps.text: Build a campfire and allow the fire to burn until a bed of hot coals has accumulated. Rake the coals into a flat bed on one side of the fire.
Meanwhile, cook ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat until browned, stirring to crumble. Discard excess fat; stir taco seasoning into beef according to package directions.

Coat inside of a pie iron with cooking spray. Place 1 corn tortilla on one side, top with 1 scoop ground beef, sprinkle with Monterey Jack cheese, add chopped onion; place 1 (more) corn tortilla on top. Close pie iron.
Cook taco over moderate campfire coals until tortillas have crisped and browned and taco is hot in center. Serve with lettuce, tomato, salsa, and sour cream. Repeat with remaining ingredients.

raw_recipe.headline: Pie Iron Tacos
raw_recipe.description: This pie iron taco recipe is cooked over a campfire in a pie iron with taco-seasoned ground beef, shredded Monterey Jack cheese, onion, and tortillas.

review.reviewBody: I can't wait to have these tomorrow when we go camping! I tried them with the pie iron but over an open flame on the stove...just to make sure it would work before I lug it all to the campground. They are delicious! I subbed flour for corn tortillas and omitted the onion. I've found a new favorite camping food! :) ****Update**** I made these camping yesterday and they we SO good! My husband couldn't believe how good they turned out...I think he was a little leery of "campfire tacos." I had precooked the beef at home so all I had to do was assemble and cook once we started our campfire. I'm sure they'll be requested whenever we camp from now on! :)

Made these while camping last weekend. We made them with chicken and cooked the meat with the taco seasoning ahead of time. My husband and I thought the were a great change of pace for camping. Made the kids with only cheese, like a pie iron quesadilla. There was some experimentation with the timing of the tacos in the pie iron. We burnt the first batch, but then got the hang of it! Thanks for the recipe!

These hobo tacos were very good while camping. We used small flour tortillas and cooked the ground beef at home before we left, which made putting it all together really easy. We used all our traditional taco fillings including olives, green chilis, tomatoes, etc. Some went inside the taco, and others on top after it was done. Delish!
This has become a new camping recipe favorite. My kids prefer it with flour tortillas, I like corn better. Very easy to do, especially since I made the seasoned beef at home.

I'm not a big fan of "traditional" mountain pies, so I was thrilled to find this recipe. I browned and seasoned the beef before we headed camping so all we had to do was make the mountain pies. We kept it really simple and cooked w/the meat & cheese and then served w/FF sour cream.

we tried both corn and flour tortillas, both were great. nice thing about the shells is that you don't have to watch them like bread, they never burned on us. we had some w/ground beef and other w/chicken. was a nice change from the usual burgers and dogs while camping.
This was yummy. We simplified it and only did the taco meat and cheese inside. Will definetely make again and bring extra to eat more and share. Thanks for the recipe.
Can you substitute guacamole for the sour cream?...also this is more like a quesadillia

I grew up calling the "pie irons," "Toastites." This was in the forties and I still have two or three of them I occasionally use. We always use leftover roast beef and gravy at home to make them. When camping, I've used them for pizza, (bread, not dough), and pie filling in them for dessert. I like the taco idea but am surprised there is no taco sauce added while cooking. I will have to try this recipe.
These were fine. They tasted good, but there wasn't anything special about them vs just grilling the shells on the grill like usual. I thought the kids would think it was more fun than it way.

This was a bit of a disappointment for us. The taste isn’t anything special and the taco shell texture makes the taste resemble a chimichanga. It was a change from the mountain pies, but we could have just as easily just ate the tacos as is.

We made these on a camping trip and served them with sour cream and salsa. While it's a good recipe and a nice break from typical camping food, next time I'd probably add peppers or use a spicier taco seasoning to give it a little more heat.
I tried these using plain bread instead of tortillas and they were really good. I didn't have any salsa so I just used ketchup.
These were awesome. We always have a pie iron meal when camping and have tried many different sandwiches and treats but I have to say after having these, we have a new favorite.
